title: Maps of the mind and old anchors
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Whose map of the world are you using?
A student summarized the intro and chapter one: everyone has their own map of the world, their own way of mapping out how they experience reality.
I said that coaches you had in your life can seem like jerks in your younger years, and that a driven coach can leave you with a strong memory and a way of seeing.

I said: you have a negative moment; you are ten years old and your father is yelling that you are no good. That moment can become an anchor you carry. I asked everyone to be sure they understood how that works.

A student asked how you remove it. I said that what a therapist generally does is a process to remove the anchor, and that I was speaking about therapy in general terms. A person with the right training is the place to go for a painful memory.
I said that I asked a question to understand what reality the other person sees, because they could answer: Jose, I do not see that, you have no data and no evidence.
I said that you can develop mantras and phrases to break a negative cycle.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one way you map the world.
Write someone whose map is different.
Write one old moment you carry and who you could talk to about it.
Write the question that checks their reality.
Write your phrase to break a cycle.

check.q: What did a student say everyone has?
choices: Their own map of the world

check.q: What did I say a therapist generally does?
choices: A process to remove a negative anchor

check.q: What did I say you can develop to break a cycle?

recap: Know your map. Check the other person's. Seek trained help for old hurts.
